selection.ownership: Envoy, Inc. (San Francisco, CA, United States; Delaware corporation). Global workplace visitor-management SaaS at envoy.com. Distinct from Envoy Proxy (CNCF) and Envoy Air (American Airlines).

research.searchCoverage: Official Envoy Workplace Client API Key (X-API-Key) and OpenAPI for GET /rest/v1/locations, GET /rest/v1/locations/{id}, GET /v1/invites; Envoy Inc San Francisco identity; dated incident search (Envoy workplace + security breach/incident) reviewed on 2026-09-13. 2023 Atlassian employee-credential access of Envoy-held Atlassian data is recorded as a historical customer-credential incident, not an Envoy platform compromise. 2025 CL0P/Oracle EBS reports concern Envoy Air, a different company. No current unresolved Envoy Inc platform breach is asserted; this is not a breach-free claim.

Official Envoy Workplace Client API Key (X-API-Key) and OpenAPI for locations/invites, Envoy Inc San Francisco identity, and dated incident search reviewed on 2026-09-13. Pinned source is the workplace SaaS at api.envoy.com, not Envoy Proxy. 2023 Atlassian employee-credential access is recorded; Envoy stated its systems were not compromised. 2025 CL0P/Oracle EBS reports concern Envoy Air, a different company. No current unresolved Envoy Inc platform breach is asserted; this is not a breach-free claim.

incidents.affectedProduct: Envoy workplace app data visible to a customer employee account (Atlassian)
incidents.affectedData: Atlassian employee directory fields and office floor plans held in Atlassian's Envoy tenant
incidents.status: historical customer-credential incident; Envoy reported no compromise of Envoy systems
incidents.remediation: Atlassian attributed access to an employee credential posted in a public repository. Envoy published log evidence that requests used that valid customer account.
incidents.residualRisk: Customer accounts with leaked credentials can still read tenant data visible to that account.

research.waiverAuthority: User waiver dated 2026-09-13 permits historical non-China incident coverage.

adaptations: Credential-only healthcheck uses official GET /rest/v1/locations rather than the pinned validator GET /v1/employees?page=1&perPage=1. The current Employees hub page is empty and retrieve-employees documents the deprecated v3 Visitors API at app.envoy.com; locations is the documented cheap authenticated read on api.envoy.com.
Native category is productivity rather than security: Envoy is workplace visitor management, and Rust CATEGORIES has no security bucket.
Path is official GET /rest/v1/locations (OpenAPI), not the Client API Key tutorial curl to /v1/locations. Returns raw Envoy JSON under data.

ids array, enabled boolean, and createdAtAfter/createdAtBefore filters are omitted because the native query template cannot express comma-joined arrays without unused inputs and boolean query encoding is not required for the list.
id is URL-encoded in GET /rest/v1/locations/{id}. Returns raw Envoy JSON under data.

locationIds array is omitted because the native query template cannot express comma-joined arrays without unused inputs. Scalar page/perPage/hostEmail/inviteeEmail/type/approvalStatus/sort/order are caller-controlled.
id is URL-encoded in GET /v1/invites/{id}, matching the pinned handler and the documented /v1/invites collection. Returns raw Envoy JSON under data.
